in-congrŭens , tis, adj.,
I.inconsistent, incongruous, unsuitable (post-Aug.): “sententia,” Plin. Ep. 4, 9, 19 : “quod est incongruens et absurdum, ut, etc.,” Lact. 3, 8, 35 . —With dat.: “Stoica disciplina pleraque est et sibi et nobis incongruens,” Gell. 12, 5, 5 .— With subject.-clause: “incongruens est in labris habere bonitatem,” Lact. 3, 16, 4 ; 12, 17, 6.— Sup., Aug. Don. Persev. 61.— * Adv.: incongrŭenter , unsuitably, Tert. de Baptism. 19.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
